sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简讯 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于 11 月 18 日在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: I am recording and it is working.
sentences.zh: 我在录音，而且设备在正常工作。

sentences.en: Hey, Tilly.
sentences.zh: 嘿，蒂莉。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm doing okay.
sentences.zh: 我挺好的。

sentences.en: Tilly, what is that in your hand?
sentences.zh: 蒂莉，你手里拿的是什么？

sentences.en: It looks like either a blanket or a stuffed animal.
sentences.zh: 看起来像是一条毯子或者一个毛绒玩具。

sentences.en: It's a blanket.
sentences.zh: 是一条毯子。

sentences.en: Oh, what does it say on it?
sentences.zh: 哦，上面写着什么？

sentences.en: It says powered by pizza.
sentences.zh: 上面写着靠披萨驱动。

sentences.en: And does it look like it has an image of pepperoni pizza on it?
sentences.zh: 而且上面看起来是不是有意大利辣香肠披萨的图案？

sentences.en: Is that what I'm glimpsing?
sentences.zh: 我没看错吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Pepperoni.
sentences.zh: 辣香肠。

sentences.en: That's pretty great.
sentences.zh: 那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Um, well, Tilly, I really want to thank you for getting on the phone with us, or I guess this Google hangout with us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，蒂莉，我真的很感谢你肯和我们通话，或者说通过这个谷歌视频通话跟我们交流。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you could tell me your full name and how old you are.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否告诉我你的全名以及你今年多大。

sentences.en: Matilda Rose BrimhorSt.
sentences.zh: 玛蒂尔达·罗斯·布里姆霍斯特。
zh_words: 玛蒂尔达·罗斯·布里姆霍斯特

sentences.en: And then I am 12.
sentences.zh: 然后我 12 岁。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I just want to start with a very simple question.
sentences.zh: 我想从一个非常简单的问题开始。

sentences.en: How have you been feeling this past week?
sentences.zh: 这过去的一周你感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Um, I'm kind of in and out of moods.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的情绪有点起伏不定。

sentences.en: Usually the two moods that I'm mostly in are sad and angry.
sentences.zh: 通常我最常有的两种情绪是伤心和生气。

sentences.en: And why do you think that you're sad and angry?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得你为什么会伤心和生气呢？

sentences.en: What about?
sentences.zh: 是为了什么？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We're, I feel like we're sad and angry because I think angry more that it's not fair that he's gone.
sentences.zh: 我们，我觉得我们会伤心和生气，是因为我觉得生气更多是因为他走了很不公平。

sentences.en: And I feel like sad is really, we're sad that he's gone and sad that we're being sad.
sentences.zh: 我觉得伤心是，我们既为他的离去感到难过，也为自己沉浸在悲伤中感到难过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: More than 50,000 Americans have died from the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 已有五万多名美国人死于冠状病毒。

sentences.en: One of them was Craig BrimhorSt. Today, his granddaughter remembers him.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是克雷格·布里姆霍斯特。今天，他的孙女在缅怀他。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 1St. I wonder if you could tell me a little bit about your grandfather.
sentences.zh: 今天是 5 月 1 日，星期五。我想请你讲讲你的祖父好吗？

sentences.en: How would you describe your grandfather physically?
sentences.zh: 你觉得从外表上看，你的祖父是个什么样的人？

sentences.en: What did he look like?
sentences.zh: 他长什么样？

sentences.en: What would he wear?
sentences.zh: 他会穿什么样的衣服？

sentences.en: Those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Well, he'd wear pastor clothes and stuff.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他会穿牧师的衣服之类的。

sentences.en: Was he a pastor?
sentences.zh: 他是个牧师吗？

sentences.en: Yes, he was a pastor.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是个牧师。

sentences.en: He used to be a mailman and then he didn't really like that job.
sentences.zh: 他以前是个邮递员，后来他觉得那份工作没那么好。

sentences.en: And he had like white hair and then the mustache that goes right into the beard.
sentences.zh: 他有一头白发，还有胡子，胡子和鬓角连在一起。

sentences.en: And when I was little, I play with his beard because it just felt so interesting touching it with my hands.
sentences.zh: 我小的时候，会玩他的胡子，因为用手摸起来感觉太有趣了。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: It felt all rough and scrapey, but like not too scrapey.
sentences.zh: 摸起来毛糙刺手，但又不是特别刺手。

sentences.en: He'd wear glasses and sometimes I stole his glasses and he's like, yeah, we bring him back.
sentences.zh: 他会戴眼镜，有时候我偷了他的眼镜，他就说，好吧，快还给我。

sentences.en: And like, whenever I walked into the house, he'd just be like, ho-dee-ho.
sentences.zh: 而且，每当我走进屋子，他就会说，呼迪呼。

sentences.en: I don't know where that came from, but just, it's always something he said.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这声音是从哪来的，但总之，这是他经常说的一句话。

sentences.en: Ho-dee-ho.
sentences.zh: 呼迪呼。

sentences.en: Ho-dee-ho.
sentences.zh: 呼迪呼。

sentences.en: It's more interesting than hello.
sentences.zh: 这比说你好有趣多了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Did he have any kind of nickname for you?
sentences.zh: 他有没有给你起过什么外号？

sentences.en: Tilly B was my one.
sentences.zh: 蒂莉·B 是我的外号。

sentences.en: Tilly B.
sentences.zh: 蒂莉·B。

sentences.en: Yeah, because for Brian Forrest, they just called me Tilly B and it kind of just rhymes.
sentences.zh: 对，因为对于布里姆霍斯特来说，他们就叫我蒂莉·B，而且听起来挺押韵的。

sentences.en: Wait, which part rhymes?
sentences.zh: 等等，哪一部分押韵？

sentences.en: Tilly and then B.
sentences.zh: 蒂莉，然后是 B。

sentences.en: It's just kind of like, it just goes together.
sentences.zh: 就感觉，它们很搭。

sentences.en: Tilly B.
sentences.zh: 蒂莉·B。

sentences.en: Tilly B.
sentences.zh: 蒂莉·B。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then he'd always make me happy.
sentences.zh: 而且他总是能让我开心。

sentences.en: I'd never like really get upset around him unless I was hurt.
sentences.zh: 在他身边我从来不会真正难过，除非我受伤了。

sentences.en: Unless you were hurt, you said.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说，除非你受伤了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because we did all sorts of crazy things.
sentences.zh: 因为我们做过各种各样疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: Wait, now I need to understand some of the crazy things you did with him.
sentences.zh: 等等，我得听听你和他一起做过的那些疯狂的事。

sentences.en: Um, well, he'd take me out on the roof once we brought sleeping bags on the roof.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他会带我到屋顶上，有一次我们把睡袋带到了屋顶上。

sentences.en: The roof of your house?
sentences.zh: 你家的屋顶？

sentences.en: Uh, no, my grandpa's house.
sentences.zh: 呃，不是，是我爷爷家。

sentences.en: But we didn't tell my dad about it until afterwards.
sentences.zh: 不过我们直到事后才告诉爸爸。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It sounds like he has a slightly mischievous quality to him.
sentences.zh: 听起来他身上有一种调皮的特质。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about that?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲吗？

sentences.en: What was that like?
sentences.zh: 那是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, it would usually be like the middle of summer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，通常是在盛夏的时候。

sentences.en: And we'd grab the stepladder and open the window, pull up the screen, climb up onto the edge of the roof, up to our special spot.
sentences.zh: 我们会拿来人字梯，打开窗户，拉起纱窗，爬到屋顶边缘，走到我们的秘密基地。

sentences.en: Just laid there on the roof.
sentences.zh: 就躺在屋顶上。

sentences.en: And we just looked at the stars and talked for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们只是看星星，聊一会儿天。

sentences.en: What kinds of things would your grandfather say?
sentences.zh: 你爷爷会说些什么？

sentences.en: Um, here, Tilly, let's look for the Big Dipper, maybe the Milky Way, if we're lucky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，来，蒂莉，我们找找北斗七星，如果运气好的话，也许还能找到银河。

sentences.en: And Mars might be like, wait, but isn't Mars a planet, not a star?
sentences.zh: 火星可能会，等等，但火星不是行星吗，不是星星？

sentences.en: You would just be like, but we can see it as a red star, kind of.
sentences.zh: 他就会说，但我们差不多可以把它看成一颗红色的星星。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The stars were really bright, and it was really warm outside.
sentences.zh: 星星真的很亮，外面非常暖和。

sentences.en: And it was beautiful.
sentences.zh: 而且非常美。

sentences.en: How often would you see your grandfather?
sentences.zh: 你多久见一次你爷爷？

sentences.en: We wouldn't see him, like, every single weekend.
sentences.zh: 我们不是每个周末都能见到他。

sentences.en: But, like, we'd see him a lot.
sentences.zh: 但是，我们会经常见面。

sentences.en: He'd, like, come to my school, and he'd sit in the lunchroom with me.
sentences.zh: 他会来我的学校，陪我一起坐在食堂吃午饭。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: He would just show up?
sentences.zh: 他会直接出现吗？

sentences.en: Did he announce himself?
sentences.zh: 他会提前通知你吗？

sentences.en: Was it unexpected?
sentences.zh: 这是意料之外的吗？

sentences.en: He would never tell me that he was coming.
sentences.zh: 他从来不告诉我他要来。

sentences.en: And he'd just be waiting for me right next to the lunchroom door, just waiting for me.
sentences.zh: 他就会在食堂门口等着我，一直在那儿等我。

sentences.en: And then I'd just look around for him every time.
sentences.zh: 然后每次我都会到处找他。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: He'd sit right next to me, and I'd have my lunchbox, and he'd kind of just pick out things from it.
sentences.zh: 他就坐在我旁边，我拿着饭盒，他就会从里面拿点东西吃。

sentences.en: Sometimes he'd take my chips, and I'd be like, Papa!
sentences.zh: 有时候他会拿我的薯片，然后我就会说，爸爸！

sentences.en: He'd talk to my friends.
sentences.zh: 他会和我的朋友们聊天。

sentences.en: He'd talk about, like, all these fun things, like all his stories about, like, going to Tanzania,
sentences.zh: 他会聊所有这些有趣的事情，比如他去坦桑尼亚的故事，

sentences.en: and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And what would you think when you saw him?
sentences.zh: 当你看到他时，心里在想什么？

sentences.en: Um, I think I'd be proud.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我会感到骄傲。

sentences.en: I'd be proud that my grandpa comes to this, to my school a lot, to just eat lunch with me and tell my friends all these stories.
sentences.zh: 我为我的爷爷经常来学校陪我吃午饭，给我的朋友们讲这些故事而感到骄傲。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: He was just there, right when I needed it, which made me feel really nice.
sentences.zh: 他就在那里，正好在我需要的时候出现，这让我感觉非常好。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't know a lot of grandpas or grandmas who'd do that.
sentences.zh: 对，我不知道有多少爷爷奶奶会这样做。

sentences.en: It's really special.
sentences.zh: 这真的很特别。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I want you to tell me, if you're willing, the story of the last few weeks and what happened with your grandfather.
sentences.zh: 所以我想让你告诉我，如果你愿意的话，过去几周的故事以及你爷爷身上发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: And I wonder, I don't know where you think we should start.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你觉得我们该从哪里开始呢。

sentences.en: Uh, I think we should, like, start from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 呃，我觉得我们应该从头开始讲。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So, Papa and my grandma went to the Holy Lambs.
sentences.zh: 所以，爸爸和奶奶去了圣地。

sentences.en: He wanted to take his church group there.
sentences.zh: 他想带他的教会团契去那里。

sentences.en: So they went to the Middle EaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他们去了中东。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Where baby Jesus was, like, born, and, like, that's the other place.
sentences.zh: 也就是小耶稣出生的地方，诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And then they got, like, this morning there, an outbreak has started here of the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 然后他们到那里那天早上，冠状病毒爆发了。

sentences.en: And so when they come back, they were straight into quarantine.
sentences.zh: 所以他们一回来，就直接开始隔离。

sentences.en: But right when they came back,
sentences.zh: 但就在他们回来的时候，

sentences.en: Papa started getting, like, really ill.
sentences.zh: 爷爷开始病得很重。

sentences.en: He had high fever, really high fever.
sentences.zh: 他发高烧，烧得很厉害。

sentences.en: And in my mind, at first when he was home, I was like, oh, he's fine.
sentences.zh: 起初他刚回家时，我心里想，哦，他没事。

sentences.en: He'll get through this.
sentences.zh: 他会挺过去的。

sentences.en: He's strong.
sentences.zh: 他很强壮。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But then he got worse and worse.
sentences.zh: 但接着他病情越来越重。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, no, it's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 我就想，哦不，要出事了。

sentences.en: And I was just kind of in a worried state.
sentences.zh: 我整个人处于一种担忧的状态。

sentences.en: But, like, not like a, oh, my gosh,
sentences.zh: 但不是那种，天哪，

sentences.en: I'm really, really sad, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我真的非常非常伤心那种状态。

sentences.en: Until, like, a couple weeks later, he just couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 直到几个星期后，他实在撑不住了。

sentences.en: And he got lifted to the hospital here.
sentences.zh: 然后他被送到这里的医院去了。

sentences.en: And, Tilly, were you talking to him during this time?
sentences.zh: 蒂莉，在这期间你跟他说话了吗？

sentences.en: No, I didn't get to talk to him at all.
sentences.zh: 没有，我根本没机会跟他说话。

sentences.en: I mean, he sent him, like, letters, but I don't know if he even got to read those.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他寄过信，但我不知道他有没有收到那些信。

sentences.en: I remember.
sentences.zh: 我记得。

sentences.en: So when I heard about that he was put in the hospital because it got worse,
sentences.zh: 所以当我听说他病情加重被送进医院时，

sentences.en: Mom was like, do you want to sleep with one of his shirts?
sentences.zh: 妈妈就问，你想抱着他的衬衫睡吗？

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I was like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我说，好啊。

sentences.en: So she brought me this shirt.
sentences.zh: 于是她把这件衬衫拿给了我。

sentences.en: It was just, like, a greenish-brown T-shirt.
sentences.zh: 它就是那种，呃，有点灰绿色的T恤。

sentences.en: Were you wearing it, or was it just beside you?
sentences.zh: 你是穿着它，还是只是把它放在旁边？

sentences.en: I was wearing it.
sentences.zh: 我穿着它。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It felt, like, really, really big on me.
sentences.zh: 我穿在身上感觉，真的，真的好大。

sentences.en: Um, it was kind of, like, cold, but it felt really soothing to wear it, though.
sentences.zh: 嗯，感觉有点凉凉的，不过穿在身上让人觉得特别安心。

sentences.en: I wanted to feel like I was close to him.
sentences.zh: 我想感受一下离他近一点的感觉。

sentences.en: I was giving him a hug, and I thought about him the whole night.
sentences.zh: 我拥抱着它，一整晚都在想他。

sentences.en: I prayed that he would make it through,
sentences.zh: 我祈祷他能挺过去，

sentences.en: that he wouldn't have to go.
sentences.zh: 祈祷他不用离开。

sentences.en: My prayer really didn't come true
sentences.zh: 我的祈祷最终没能实现，

sentences.en: because he had a stroke during the night from a heart disease that he had,
sentences.zh: 因为他本身有心脏病，结果在夜里中风了，

sentences.en: and that made it super worse.
sentences.zh: 这让情况变得极其糟糕。

sentences.en: And even if we did get him back, he wouldn't actually, like, his body would be there, but he wouldn't be there.
sentences.zh: 而且就算我们真的把他救回来了，他其实——他的身体还在，但他的人已经不在了。

sentences.en: He couldn't do anything.
sentences.zh: 他什么也做不了。

sentences.en: Like, he couldn't talk into the things that made him, him.
sentences.zh: 比如，他说不出那些构成真正独特的他的话。

sentences.en: And how did you learn the news?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么得知这个消息的？

sentences.en: Mom got a call,
sentences.zh: 妈妈接了个电话，

sentences.en: and then I looked at her, and I saw worry, so I kind of just, um, just did stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后我看着她，从她脸上看到了担忧，所以我差不多就，呃，只是做我自己的事。

sentences.en: And then Mommy told me what happened.
sentences.zh: 接着妈妈就把发生的事情告诉我了。

sentences.en: And what did she tell you?
sentences.zh: 她对你说了什么？

sentences.en: She told me about the living will that my grandma, my dad, and my uncles read it.
sentences.zh: 她跟我讲了生前预嘱的事，那是我的外公（或爷爷）、爸爸和叔叔们读过的。

sentences.en: Well, the doctor read it to them.
sentences.zh: 哦，是医生读给他们听的。

sentences.en: That it said that if something happened, he wanted to go.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，如果出了什么事，他希望能离开。

sentences.en: He didn't want to, like, have to suffer in this state.
sentences.zh: 他不想，呃，不得不带着这种状态受苦。

sentences.en: So your grandfather had written a will that made clear that if he got very sick and he'd reached a condition where things weren't working out, that he wanted to be allowed to die.
sentences.zh: 所以你外公（或爷爷）写下了一份遗嘱，清楚地表达了如果他病得很重，到了无法挽回的地步，他希望能够安乐死（或：顺其自然地离去）。

sentences.en: Yeah, and he just wanted to go to heaven and be with God.
sentences.zh: 对，他只想去天堂和上帝在一起。

sentences.en: Like he says, he wanted to fall in the arms of God.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，他想落入上帝的怀抱。

sentences.en: That's what he wrote.
sentences.zh: 他是这么写的。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wants to fall in the arms of God.
sentences.zh: 对，他想投入上帝的怀抱。

sentences.en: He's like a trust fall, really.
sentences.zh: 这真有点像信任倒（trust fall）的游戏。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I couldn't handle, like, knowing that.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法接受，呃，得知这个消息。

sentences.en: But I knew that he wouldn't be coming.
sentences.zh: 但我知道他不会回来了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And that was hard to know.
sentences.zh: 这很难接受。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: How are you holding up over there?
sentences.zh: 你那边现在感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm okay.
sentences.zh: 我挺好的。

sentences.en: It's hard talking about it, but it also makes me happy to talk about how great he was and what happened.
sentences.zh: 谈论这些很难，但同时，聊起他有多么伟大以及发生的那些事，也让我觉得很高兴。

sentences.en: You know, I've lost my grandparents, too.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我也失去过祖父母。

sentences.en: It's one of the kind of sad, inevitable things that it means to be alive is that the people before you die, and it's just really hard.
sentences.zh: 这是人生中某种悲伤但又无可避免的事情，这意味着你身边的长辈会离世，这真的很难面对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It is really hard.
sentences.zh: 确实非常难。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I want you to know you're being very brave in telling the story.
sentences.zh: 我想让你知道，你在讲这个故事时非常勇敢。

sentences.en: I know how difficult it must be.
sentences.zh: 我知道这一定很难。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你的第一个月应用体验是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间去突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》App并获得30天的免费访问权限吧。

sentences.en: Can I ask you to describe sadness to me?
sentences.zh: 我能请你向我描述一下悲伤吗？

sentences.en: What that feels like?
sentences.zh: 那是一种什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: I feel like it's hard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很难。

sentences.en: Sadness is probably a hard one for me.
sentences.zh: 对我和说，悲伤可能是一个很难描述的概念。

sentences.en: Happiness, I could do easily, but sadness is kind of hard.
sentences.zh: 快乐我可以轻松表达，但悲伤有点难。

sentences.en: Why is happiness easy, and why is sadness hard, do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得为什么快乐很简单，而悲伤却很难呢？

sentences.en: Um, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, sadness is an emotion that is kind of, like, more, like, deeper, and it's kind of, like, a big, big emotion.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，悲伤这种情绪有点，怎么说，更加深沉，它算是一种很大很大的情绪。

sentences.en: Happiness can be big, but not as much as sadness.
sentences.zh: 快乐也可以很大，但没有悲伤那么强烈。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: There's a depth to it that makes it hard to describe.
sentences.zh: 它有一种深度，让人很难去描述。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I just kind of feel like sadness is, like,
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得悲伤有点像，

sentences.en: just an ocean filled with nothing.
sentences.zh: 就像是一片空无一物的海洋。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Have you noticed that the people around you, your parents, that they are sad, too?
sentences.zh: 你有没有发现你身边的人，你的父母，他们也很伤心？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So,
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: my dad will go outside a lot.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸会经常去外面。

sentences.en: You can tell that he's getting angry, and he's really short-tempered.
sentences.zh: 你能看出他在变生气的，而且他的脾气变得很急躁。

sentences.en: At that point, mom will kind of just stay in her office, not really doing anything, but she'll just sit around.
sentences.zh: 到了那个时候，妈妈基本上就会待在她的办公室里，什么也不做，只是坐在那里消磨时间。

sentences.en: Like, I've seen mom try to keep crying to herself, and dad, too, but I can see it.
sentences.zh: 比如，我见过妈妈试图偷偷哭泣，爸爸也是，但我都能看出来。

sentences.en: You mean try to, they're trying to shield it from you?
sentences.zh: 你是说他们试图——他们是在试图向你隐瞒吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But I can still feel it.
sentences.zh: 但我依然能感受到。

sentences.en: Do you wish that they would just do it in front of you?
sentences.zh: 你希望他们直接在你面前表现出来吗？

sentences.en: Do you?
sentences.zh: 你希望吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do.
sentences.zh: 希望。

sentences.en: And why do you think they should do it more out in the open?
sentences.zh: 你为什么觉得他们应该更公开地表现出来呢？

sentences.en: I kind of feel like I can, it helps me understand my emotions as well.
sentences.zh: 我感觉这样能，这也有助于我理解自己的情绪。

sentences.en: Like, how they feel.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们的感受是什么样的。

sentences.en: Do I feel that?
sentences.zh: 我是不是也有这种感觉？

sentences.en: It kind of gives you permission to feel the way you feel.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上给了你允许自己去感受当下情绪的权力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like, when I was talking to my dad about Papa, he started crying, and I started crying, and then we just hugged, and it was nice.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我跟爸爸谈起外公（或爷爷）时，他开始哭，我也开始哭，然后我们抱在了一起，那种感觉很好。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of kids are going through what you're going through right now because of this virus, and a lot of adults are going through this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为这场病毒，很多孩子都在经历你现在所经历的事，许多成年人也在经历这些。

sentences.en: I wonder how that makes you feel.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这让你有什么感受？

sentences.en: It makes me feel, like, not alone, and it also kind of makes me feel a bit angry about how they still haven't figured out how this started.
sentences.zh: 这让我觉得，我不是一个人，但同时这也让我感到有点生气，因为他们到现在还没搞清楚这到底是怎么开始的。

sentences.en: I want to know so I could figure out, like, how it wouldn't happen again.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这样我才能弄清楚怎么才能避免这种事再次发生。

sentences.en: Like, was it a cause of a human that did it?
sentences.zh: 比如，这是人类造成的吗？

sentences.en: Was it a cause of an animal?
sentences.zh: 是动物引起的吗？

sentences.en: Or was it kind of both?
sentences.zh: 还是说两者兼有？

sentences.en: And if it turns out this is just something that nature and the universe gave us, and it wasn't somebody who did something, how would you feel about that?
sentences.zh: 如果最后发现这只是大自然和宇宙给我们的一场考验，而不是某个人做了什么导致的，你对此会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I'd be mad at the universe.
sentences.zh: 我会生宇宙的气。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I know that a lot of people, when someone they care about or they love passes away, they end up looking for that person in the world, or they end up thinking about that person
sentences.zh: 我知道很多人在他们关心或爱的人离世后，最终会在世界上寻找那个人的身影，或者他们会不由自主地想起那个人，

sentences.en: unexpectedly.
sentences.zh: 在完全意想不到的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Thinking that maybe they're there or they're standing by you, that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 会觉得也许他们在那里，或者正站在你身边，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel like
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得

sentences.en: Papa was, like, by me a lot, but sometimes I feel like he's out there, like, with other people
sentences.zh: 外公（或爷爷）以前经常陪在我身边，但有时我觉得他在外面，比如跟其他人在一起，

sentences.en: and, uh,
sentences.zh: 然后，呃，

sentences.en: helping them through their bad moments.
sentences.zh: 帮他们度过糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, I have
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我

sentences.en: a very specific
sentences.zh: 有着一种非常深刻的

sentences.en: sense of my grandmother whenever
sentences.zh: 对奶奶的记忆，每当

sentences.en: this song comes on, because when I was around your age, she died, and a song was playing on the radio, and it was a song that made me feel
sentences.zh: 这首歌响起时，因为在我像你这么大时，她去世了，当时收音机里正播着一首歌，那首歌让我觉得

sentences.en: sad, even though it was a love song.
sentences.zh: 很悲伤，尽管它是一首情歌。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've ever heard this song.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有听过这首歌。

sentences.en: It's by Richard Varks, and it goes, wherever you go, whatever you do, I will be right there waiting for you.
sentences.zh: 那是理查·马克斯（Richard Marx）唱的，歌词是：无论你走向何方，无论你做什么，我都会在那里守候着你。

sentences.en: And
sentences.zh: 而

sentences.en: it always makes me think of my grandmother and her death whenever it comes on.
sentences.zh: 每当这首歌响起时，它总是让我想起我的奶奶以及她的离去。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you're having moments like that yet.
sentences.zh: 我在想你是不是也有过这样的时刻。

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 对，

sentences.en: I do have those type of moments, but, like, kind of different than just a song.
sentences.zh: 我确实有过那种时刻，不过，呃，跟单纯的一首歌有点不太一样。

sentences.en: It's more of when I saw my grandma in her backyard, because we went over just to the backyard.
sentences.zh: 更多时候是在我看到外婆（或奶奶）在后院里的时候，因为我们当时只是去了后院。

sentences.en: We weren't allowed to get close to anyone, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我们不允许靠近任何人。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I felt, I felt like he, I felt, like, sad, sad, but I also felt kind of, kind of relieved that he's, is in peace now.
sentences.zh: 我当时感觉，我感觉他，我感觉，呃，非常非常难过，但我也觉得有种，有种如释重负的感觉，因为他现在平静了。

sentences.en: He didn't have to deal with this bad virus.
sentences.zh: 他不用再去应付这个糟糕的病毒了。

sentences.en: He doesn't have to feel pain or sadness or anything.
sentences.zh: 他不必再感受痛苦、悲伤或任何别的东西。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Tilly, have you gone outside and looked up at the stars since your grandfather died?
sentences.zh: 蒂莉，自从你外公（或爷爷）去世后，你有去外面抬头看过星星吗？

sentences.en: Um, only a little bit, but not much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就看了一点点，没看太多。

sentences.en: It's not the same without being at my grandma's house.
sentences.zh: 不在外婆（或奶奶）家的话，感觉就不一样了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Do you think that you, you will do that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你，你会去那样做吗？

sentences.en: Do you think there'll be a point when you'll want to do that?
sentences.zh: 你觉得会有那么一个时刻，你想去做这件事吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 会的。

sentences.en: We said when we're gonna go over to grandma's house, um, me, daddy, and my big sister are gonna go up onto the roof
sentences.zh: 我们说过，等我们去外婆（或奶奶）家的时候，呃，我和爸爸还有我姐姐要一起去屋顶上，

sentences.en: and just sit there looking at the stars.
sentences.zh: 就坐在那里看星星。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 那个，

sentences.en: Tilly, I really want to thank you for spending
sentences.zh: 蒂莉，我真的很想谢谢你

sentences.en: time with us.
sentences.zh: 抽空和我们聊聊。

sentences.en: And I want to tell you
sentences.zh: 我也想对你说，

sentences.en: I'm sorry I am about the loss of your grandfather.
sentences.zh: 得知你祖父去世的消息，我感到非常难过。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It was really good to talk to you.
sentences.zh: 能和你聊聊真的很好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: It feels good to talk to someone about it.
sentences.zh: 能和别人聊聊这事，感觉好多了。

sentences.en: It's good to talk.
sentences.zh: 聊聊挺好的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: The latest data from the Labor Department shows that more than
sentences.zh: 劳工部的最新数据显示，自疫情爆发以来，

sentences.en: 30 million Americans have filed for unemployment benefits since the start of the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 已有超过三千万美国人申请了失业救济金。

sentences.en: But the Times reports that the real figure is probably much higher.
sentences.zh: 但《时报》报道称，实际数字可能要高得多。

sentences.en: A new study found that about 8 million more Americans have either failed or not even tried to apply for unemployment, meaning that close to
sentences.zh: 一项新的研究发现，大约还有八千万美国人未能申请或甚至根本没有尝试申请失业救济，这意味着

sentences.en: 40 million may now be unemployed.
sentences.zh: 目前失业人数可能接近四千万。

sentences.en: and
sentences.zh: 而且

sentences.en: President Trump is letting the federal guidelines for social distancing, which were put in place in mid-March, expire as of this morning.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统正让三月中旬出台的联邦保持社交距离指导方针于今天上午过期失效。

sentences.en: I think a way of saying it, they'll be fading out because now the governors are doing it.
sentences.zh: 我想换个说法，它们会逐渐淡出，因为现在各州长正在接手。

sentences.en: I've had many calls from governors, governor of Texas.
sentences.zh: 我接到了很多州长的电话，比如德克萨斯州州长。

sentences.en: During a meeting in the Oval Office,
sentences.zh: 在椭圆形办公室的一次会议期间，

sentences.en: Trump said that responsibility for social distancing would now fall to governors.
sentences.zh: 特朗普表示，保持社交距离的责任现在将落到各州长身上。

sentences.en: I am very much in favor of what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 我非常赞成他们正在做的事情。

sentences.en: They're getting it going and we're opening our country again.
sentences.zh: 他们正在行动起来，我们正在重新开放我们的国家。

sentences.en: Do you want to explain that, please?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗，拜托？

sentences.en: Finally, we are doing a lot of things here that we've never done before, but this is as ambitious as anything that we've ever undertaken.
sentences.zh: 最后，我们在这里做了很多以前从未做过的事情，但这和我们以往承办的任何事情一样宏大。

sentences.en: In New York, officials said that the New York
sentences.zh: 在纽约，官员们表示，纽约

sentences.en: City subway system, the only system in the country that runs 24 hours a day, will now be shut down every night between 1 and 5 a.m.
sentences.zh: 市地铁系统是全国唯一一个全天候二十四小时运行的系统，现在将在每天凌晨一点到五点之间关闭，

sentences.en: so that trains can be disinfected.
sentences.zh: 以便对列车进行消毒。

sentences.en: We have the essential workers who we are so grateful to because they're coming to work every day.
sentences.zh: 我们有我们非常感激的杰出工作者，因为他们每天都来上班。

sentences.en: We all say thank you, but gratitude is best acted upon, right?
sentences.zh: 我们都说着谢谢，但感恩最好付诸行动，对吧？

sentences.en: I want to know that they have safe, clean, decent transportation and that means we have to disinfect the trains every 24 hours the virus...
sentences.zh: 我想确保他们有安全、干净、体面的交通工具，这意味着我们必须每二十四小时对列车进行一次消毒，以防病毒……

sentences.en: The subway has shut down just twice in the past decade, both times when it was flooded during hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 在过去的十年里，地铁只关闭过两次，两次都是在飓风发洪水的时候。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时甚至令人兴奋的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都会》（Metro）中，我和萨姆·科尼格一起，为您讲述人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
